1#main: The law of one who buys an animal from a gentile and does not know if it previously gave birth. In it are 6 seifim. One who buys an animal from a gentile and it is unknown whether it previously gave birth and bore—behold it is a doubtful firstborn and is eaten in its blemished state by the owners and is not for the kohen, for the burden of proof is on the one who extracts from his fellow—whether he bought it within its year or after its year. And even if the gentile speaks offhand that it already gave birth, he is not believed. (And signs in the cracks of its horns do not raise or lower to rely on them (Hagahos Mordechai, chapter HaIshah).)
2#main: If he bought a nursing animal from a gentile, he is not concerned lest it is nursing another's offspring; rather it is presumed to have given birth. And even if what it nurses is like another species, and even like swine—it is exempt from the firstborn.
3#main: And likewise an animal that is milking is exempt from the firstborn, for most animals do not milk unless they gave birth. {Rama: And some say one does not rely on the fact that it is milking (Tur in the name of the Geonim and Hagahos Mordechai, chapter HaIshah). And the later authorities ruled thus (Maharai in his rulings siman 166, Terumat HaDeshen siman 271, Mahariu siman 174). And so is the custom in all these lands. Nevertheless, if there is another side to permit—such as a gentile speaking offhand not to enhance his sale and saying it gave birth—one may rely to permit; and specifically with cows, in a place where it is not heard that they milk without offspring; but with goats, where the custom is to milk without offspring, we do not rely on this—even in a place where there is a double doubt, such as if it bore two and one might say one ate the other and it is not a firstborn—nevertheless it is forbidden (Piskei Maharai siman 130). And it appears to me that in a place where goats are not accustomed thus, or where cows are accustomed thus, one need not distinguish, and one should investigate this.}
4#main: An animal that we saw milking and we know it did not give birth—if afterward we saw it nursing and we do not know if that offspring is its own or not, behold it is presumed to have given birth to it.
5#main: One who has in his flock animals that previously gave birth and those that did not, and they gave birth and no person was there, and he finds those that previously gave birth nursing females and those that did not nursing males—he is not concerned lest this one's offspring came to that one and that one's to this; rather the matter is in its presumption that each nurses its own offspring.
6#main: One who buys an animal from an Israelite—behold it is presumed to have previously given birth, until the seller informs him it has not yet given birth. (And some say it is a doubtful firstborn (Tur in the name of the Rosh and R' Yonah).)
